clue.text: After very little time, companion needs a drink

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a very short time
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Somebody stops for a moment, then their friend wants something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts CH and A behind MO, the short moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a strong coffee, originally from the Yemeni port, so it is a kind of hot beverage.

clue.text: Mother takes up new look, concealing identity as outlaw's sweetheart

indicators.note: concealing means holding hidden inside

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
ID is short for identity

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up lifts the letters, so they are read bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A mother adopts a fresh appearance to disguise herself as a bandit's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes up' turns N and AIR into RIAN after MAMA; 'concealing' hides ID within, after the first MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid Marian is Robin Hood's beloved in English legend, the outlaw's sweetheart.

clue.text: Officer discovered route through mountains

definitions.meaning: The abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
a pass or saddle between mountain peaks

explanation.surface: An officer finds a pass through the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the colonel abbreviation for an officer, and a mountain pass for the route.

clue.text: First-class food and drink provided on train

parts.note: A denotes first-class, as in A1
board means meals, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Railway passengers in first class get meals included.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard is being on a vehicle, so on board a train.

clue.text: Freshly-minted dime and notes produced as legal tender

indicators.note: newly struck coins are remade, signalling that the letters are recast in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Newly struck coins and banknotes are issued as currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly-minted' turns DIME and NOTES into new shapes; the money surface keeps the anagram hidden in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To monetise something is to give it the status of currency, so the verb fits being made legal money.

clue.text: Compiler's witty remark about Murdoch, perhaps, being biographical writer

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to himself as me, with 's meaning is

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a mot is a witty saying, as in bon mot
Iris Murdoch was a novelist; perhaps flags her first name as an example

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's quip about the media tycoon Murdoch makes him a biographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murdoch, perhaps' suggests Rupert the newspaper owner, but it is the novelist Iris; 'about' puts IRIS inside MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A memoirist writes memoirs, life writing about themselves or others, so a biographical author.

clue.text: Sikes's girl seen in French city

definitions.meaning: Bill Sikes's lover in Dickens's Oliver Twist
a city in Lorraine, north-east France

explanation.surface: Bill Sikes's girlfriend is spotted in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings fit: the girl in Oliver Twist and the city of Lorraine in France share the name.

clue.text: Talking of food, use tool to dig up edible tuber

indicators.note: talking asks us to say the word and write what is heard

parts.note: tucker is Australian slang for food
to hoe is to break up the soil with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Speaking of things to eat, get a garden tool to unearth a root crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking of' marks a soundalike: TUCKER, Australian slang for food, is said like TUCKA, and HOE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuckahoe is a North American root or fungus eaten by Native Americans, an edible tuber.

clue.text: Cash pool you ultimately invested in films

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, a money pun

parts.note: slicks are thin films, as of oil on water
a pond is a pool

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Money pooled by investors is put into the movie business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'films' suggests cinema, but it means slicks; 'invested in' puts POND and U inside SLICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spondulicks is old slang for money, so it means cash.

clue.text: Opinion of old mistress?

definitions.meaning: an opinion or doctrine, as in orthodoxy
an archaic word for a lover or kept woman

explanation.surface: Asking what someone thinks of an ageing lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a doctrine held, and an old term for a mistress.

clue.text: Films one shot going round a possession of the Crown

indicators.note: the scrambled letters surround the A, as something going round encloses it
shot means wrecked or ruined, telling us the letters of the first two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone shoots a film by circling a single point with the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles FILMS and ONE, and 'going round' wraps that jumble round A.
explanation.definitionFit: The island in the Irish Sea is a Crown dependency, owned by the British monarch rather than part of the UK.

clue.text: Say, go for this sort of pastry

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word out loud and spell what it sounds like

parts.note: shoo is a command telling someone to go away

explanation.surface: A baker urges someone to try a particular type of pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks a soundalike: SHOO, an order to go, is pronounced the same as the French pastry name.
explanation.definitionFit: Choux is the light pastry used for eclairs and profiteroles, so it is a sort of pastry.

clue.text: Setting for end-of-term production?

parts.note: reads like a school play at the end of term, but the term is a pregnancy and the production is a baby being born

explanation.surface: Where the school stages its play at the end of the academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital ward where babies are delivered is the place a full-term pregnancy ends in birth.

clue.text: Could they be great risks, swimming round end of beach?

definitions.text: Could they be great risks, swimming round end of beach?

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters enclose the other piece
swimming suggests moving about, so the letters are mixed up
end of points to the last letter of beach

explanation.surface: Asking whether swimming near the shoreline poses big dangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' mixes GREAT RISKS and 'round' encloses H, the last letter of 'beach'; the whole clue also describes the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger sharks are large predatory fish found near coasts, plausibly dangerous to swimmers by a beach.

clue.text: Member of family needing car to be fixed

indicators.note: something to be fixed must be put right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative whose car needs repairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be fixed' rearranges NEEDING CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandniece is the granddaughter of one's sibling, so a relative.

clue.text: Piece of jazz with a characteristic pattern of notes

parts.note: a rag is a piece of ragtime, an early jazz style

explanation.surface: A jazz tune built around a signature sequence of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian classical music a raga is a melodic framework with its own set pattern of notes.

clue.text: Who might be more excited, catching female bird?

definitions.text: Who might be more excited, catching female bird?

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: wilder means more excited or more frenzied
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A question about who gets most worked up when a hen is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts F and OWL inside WILDER; the whole clue also describes the answer, a hunter thrilled to bag a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildfowler hunts ducks and geese, so would be the one excited at catching a bird.

clue.text: With which parson takes the lead?

definitions.text: With which parson takes the lead?

parts.words: With which parson takes the lead?
parts.note: suggests a priest leading, but a dog's lead clips onto a collar, and clergy wear one

explanation.surface: Asking what a vicar uses when he leads the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy wear a stiff white band at the neck, named after what a pet wears for its leash.

clue.text: Housebreaker? One turned out right in the end

indicators.note: in the end places the abbreviation for right last

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the word turned is rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar turned out to be right at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TURNED into NTRUDE, and 'in the end' puts R last.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder enters a property without permission, so a burglar is one kind.

clue.text: Suitable location for production of Pinafore?

definitions.text: Suitable location for production of Pinafore?

parts.words: Suitable location for production of Pinafore?
parts.note: reads as a theatre to stage Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore, but a pinafore is an apron, so the stage is named after one

explanation.surface: Asking which theatre would suit a staging of the operetta HMS Pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; a pinafore is also an apron.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron stage juts out in front of the curtain, a theatre location punningly fitted to an apron-themed show.

clue.text: Current Tory sex symbol?

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: Asking whether the present Conservative politician is a heart-throb.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a celebrated figure, so a sex symbol is an idolised star in that sense.

clue.text: Does one struggle to eat poultry product?

definitions.text: Does one struggle to eat poultry product?

indicators.note: eat means take in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
an egg is produced by hens

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone finds it hard to eat an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts EGG inside VIE; the whole clue also asks whether a vegetarian may eat eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A veggie is a vegetarian, who may well wonder whether eggs are allowed.

clue.text: Naval commander's address in timeless Cornwall town

indicators.note: in places the speech inside the trimmed town name
timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: Helston is a market town in Cornwall, in south-west England
an oration is a formal speech or address

explanation.surface: An admiral gives a speech in an old Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T from HELSTON to leave HELSON, and 'in' places ORATION inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The British admiral who won at Trafalgar is the most famous naval commander in British history.

clue.text: Award-winning journalist was fond of the booze?

parts.note: top means best, as a prizewinner is
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A prizewinning reporter liked a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'journalist' as ED is the crossword shorthand for editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is to drink alcohol heavily, so toped means drank habitually.

clue.text: Steal cat

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to steal a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both fit: whip as slang for pinch, and the cat as a flogging whip.

clue.text: Man with long straight stick as ruler

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
a rod is a long straight stick

explanation.surface: A man wielding a long rod in the manner of a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick to match the rod, but it means a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod was the king of Judaea in the Gospels, a biblical ruler.

clue.text: Noble friend's final resting place

parts.note: a pal is a friend, with the possessive giving the S
a grave is where someone is finally laid to rest

explanation.surface: A nobleman visits the tomb of a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A palsgrave was a German count palatine, a title of nobility.

clue.text: A Mafia member finally avoided trouble

indicators.note: finally avoided means dropping the last letter of the word

parts.note: a don is a Mafia boss

explanation.surface: A gangster at last steered clear of difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally avoided' drops N from DON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, so trouble in the sense of much ado.

clue.text: Old mailman, one stepping out by side of river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a strider is someone walking with long steps

explanation.surface: A postman of yesteryear walks along the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by side of' just sets the walker next to the river name.
explanation.definitionFit: A postrider was a mounted courier carrying the mail, an old-style mailman.

clue.text: Useful knowledge about English verse form

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for knowledge is read backwards

parts.note: dope is slang for useful inside information

explanation.surface: Handy facts concerning a form of English poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DOPE into EPOD before E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An epode is a lyric poem form, especially the third part of a Greek ode.
